newsitem.title: USA: Cracked cylinder blamed for Mir fire.
newsitem.headline: Cracked cylinder blamed for Mir fire.

text.p: A fire aboard the Russian space station Mir appeared to have been caused by a cracked lithium perchlorate cylinder used in oxygen-generation and could not be blammed on the age of the station, Frank Culbertson, an astronaut who heads NASA's shuttle-Mir program, said on Monday.
"It was a consumable that is periodically replenished on the Mir that appeared to have the problem," he said. "I wouldn't tie that to Mir life expectancy at all."

The fire occurred on Sunday while the 12-year-old space station, the world's only permanent orbiting craft, was out of radio contact and it was an hour before the crew could inform the Russian mission control, Culbertson said.

The six cosmonauts, including American Jerry Linenger, wore oxygen-generating gear for about 20 minutes after the accident and then switched to gas masks and air filters. Culbertson said they would wear the masks overnight as a precaution.
In Moscow officials said the crew was in no danger from the seven-minute blaze in an air filtering unit that released fumes irritating the crew's throats.
An officer with Russia's military space forces said the Mir blaze was "not a serious incident."
"There was no need to evacuate the Mir crew," he said.
Culberston said Linenger's wife, Kathryn, who is expecting their second child in June, was informed of the fire.
"She understood what was going on and she was fine," Culberston said.
He said the Russian space authorities would start a formal investigation into the incident.
